:::{#exm-wcgs-intercept}

#### The fitted WCGS intercept as a log-odds

The code below compares the intercept of the fitted model (`chd_glm_contrasts`) with the predicted log-odds for a type B participant at age 0,
and compares $\expf{\hat\beta_0}$ with the corresponding predicted odds:

```{r}
#| label: exm-wcgs-intercept-calc
#| code-fold: show
ex_new <- data.frame(
  dibpat = factor("Type B", levels = levels(wcgs$dibpat)),
  age = 0
)
ex_eta <- predict(chd_glm_contrasts, newdata = ex_new, type = "link")
ex_prob <- predict(chd_glm_contrasts, newdata = ex_new, type = "response")
ex_odds <- ex_prob / (1 - ex_prob)
ex_b0 <- unname(coef(chd_glm_contrasts)["(Intercept)"])
```

The intercept is `r round(ex_b0, 4)`
and the predicted log-odds is `r round(unname(ex_eta), 4)`.
Also, $\expf{\hat\beta_0}$ is `r signif(exp(ex_b0), 3)`
and the predicted odds is `r signif(unname(ex_odds), 3)`.
These values are tiny because age 0 lies far outside the observed ages,
so the intercept is an extrapolation.

:::
